datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) Relative Humidity Sensor (RHS) and Ground Temperature Sensor (GTS) measurements (publicly available on NASA Planetary Data System, Planetary Atmospheres Node)
datasets.instrument_sensor: REMS (Rover Environmental Monitoring Station); RHS (Relative Humidity Sensor); GTS (Ground Temperature Sensor)
datasets.measurement_observable: Air relative humidity with respect to ice at 1.6 m height (RHi_a) and air temperature (Ta) from RHS; ground temperature (Tg) derived from GTS infrared radiance; inferred ground relative humidity (RHi_g and RHl_g) and inferred water vapor pressure (PH2O) used for comparison to Ca(ClO4)2 deliquescence/efflorescence phase boundaries
datasets.wavelength_bandpass: GTS infrared bands: 8–14 µm, 15.5–19 µm, and 14.5–15.5 µm
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ meteorological time-series measurements (humidity, air temperature, ground temperature)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: First 1648 sols of MSL mission; specific sols highlighted: sol 1232 (Ls 99°) and sol 1311 (Ls 137°)
datasets.location_coverage: Gale crater, Mars (landing on floor at 4.7°S, 137°E); along Curiosity traverse; highlighted points occurred while rover was near active sand dunes; RHS at 1.6 m height; GTS field of view covers ~100 m^2 depending on geometry
datasets.temporal_resolution_cadence: REMS nominal strategy: 5 min of measurements at 1 Hz every Mars hour, with interspersed full-hour sample periods at 1 Hz; analysis uses only first 4 s after RHS turn-on after ≥~5 min inactivity; derived ~24 hourly values per sol under nominal strategy; GTS averaged over 5-min intervals centered on simultaneous RHS measurements (≥60 GTS samples)
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: "Updated calibrations" to REMS data (no PDS processing level stated); analysis further filters to highest-confidence measurements (e.g., specific GTS quality and no shadows)
datasets.how_used: Selected high-confidence, simultaneous hourly RHS (RHi_a, Ta) and GTS-derived Tg measurements (first 1648 sols) to infer ground humidity (RHl_g and RHi_g) and compare humidity–temperature conditions against the Ca(ClO4)2 phase diagram to assess whether surface deliquescence/brine formation is permitted; highlighted potential near-threshold cases on sols 1232 and 1311.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) measurements used to infer nighttime surface enthalpy changes (publicly available on NASA Planetary Data System, Planetary Atmospheres Node)
datasets.instrument_sensor: REMS (Rover Environmental Monitoring Station); RHS (Relative Humidity Sensor); GTS (Ground Temperature Sensor)
datasets.measurement_observable: REMS-measured surface/ground temperatures (Tg) and inferred water vapor pressure at 1.6 m (PH2O inferred from RHi_a and Ta) to compute slopes in 1/Tg vs ln(PH2O) space and derive enthalpy changes (ΔH) for near-surface phase processes
datasets.wavelength_bandpass: GTS infrared bands: 8–14 µm, 15.5–19 µm, and 14.5–15.5 µm
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ meteorological time-series measurements (used to derive thermodynamic/enthalpy time series)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: First 1648 sols (nighttime analysis); data binned over 5 sols; time spans evaluated: midnight–3 a.m., 3–6 a.m., 6–9 a.m., 6–9 p.m., and 9 p.m.–midnight; significant ΔH primarily around Ls ~100°
datasets.location_coverage: Gale crater, Mars; Curiosity traverse; uses REMS-derived water vapor pressure at 1.6 m and REMS-measured surface temperatures
datasets.temporal_resolution_cadence: Uses REMS time-series to build vapor pressure curves; data binned over 5 sols for each 3-hr time span (nighttime/early morning intervals)
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Uses REMS measurements with propagated measurement error; no PDS processing level stated
datasets.how_used: Constructed nighttime vapor-pressure curves from REMS Tg and inferred PH2O (from RHS) to estimate statistically significant enthalpy changes (ΔH) as potential signatures of near-surface processes (e.g., sublimation/condensation and possibly deliquescence) and to contextualize the rare near-threshold deliquescence cases.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) derived water vapor pressure and surface meteorology used as boundary condition/validation for subsurface heat–mass transfer modeling (publicly available on NASA Planetary Data System, Planetary Atmospheres Node)
datasets.measurement_observable: Fits to REMS-derived water vapor pressure defining water vapor just above regolith for a surface-atmosphere mass conservation boundary condition; simulated surface temperature/relative humidity compared to REMS-derived surface values for model validation
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ meteorological measurements used to force/validate a subsurface model (derived boundary-condition time series)
datasets.location_coverage: Gale crater, Mars; REMS-derived near-surface water vapor used at the surface-atmosphere interface to couple observations to a 1-D subsurface heat and mass transfer model
datasets.how_used: Used REMS-derived water vapor pressure (via fits) to set the near-surface water vapor boundary condition in a coupled subsurface heat and mass transfer simulation and compared simulated surface temperature/relative humidity against surface-derived REMS values to validate the model before assessing subsurface deliquescence potential.

output_parsed.paper_title: Constraining the Potential Liquid Water Environment at Gale Crater, Mars

queries.query: Locate the Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity) REMS raw (EDR) in situ meteorology time series for Gale crater covering roughly the first ~1600 sols, specifically the Relative Humidity Sensor air relative humidity (with respect to ice) and air temperature at the mast plus the Ground Temperature Sensor infrared-derived ground temperature, to reconstruct near-surface humidity–temperature phase space relevant to Ca-perchlorate deliquescence constraints.

Locate the Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity) REMS processed (RDR) in situ environmental records for Gale crater spanning the early mission (order of the first ~1600 sols), providing physical-unit meteorology suitable for diurnal/seasonal water-activity analyses (e.g., converting humidity with respect to ice to liquid-relative humidity and screening for near-eutectic temperature/humidity windows).

output_parsed.paper_title: Constraining the Potential Liquid Water Environment at Gale Crater, Mars

queries.query: Assemble MSL Curiosity REMS raw (EDR-level) time-series from Gale crater spanning the first ~1648 sols, specifically the relative humidity sensor measurements referenced to ice together with simultaneous ground temperature sensor readings, to reconstruct near-surface water vapor pressure and quantify nighttime latent-heat/enthalpy behavior using 1/Tg versus ln(PH2O) slope fits binned over multi-sol intervals.

Compile MSL Curiosity REMS processed (RDR-level) environmental records in physical units for Gale crater over the early multi-year traverse, including corrected air temperature/relative humidity and ground IR brightness temperatures, to test humidity–temperature crossings relevant to calcium-perchlorate deliquescence and to map seasonal/diurnal windows (e.g., around Ls ~100) when near-surface liquids could be thermodynamically permitted.

final_output.query: Locate the Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity) REMS raw (EDR) in situ meteorology time series for Gale crater covering roughly the first ~1600 sols, specifically the Relative Humidity Sensor air relative humidity (with respect to ice) and air temperature at the mast plus the Ground Temperature Sensor infrared-derived ground temperature, to reconstruct near-surface humidity–temperature phase space relevant to Ca-perchlorate deliquescence constraints.

Locate the Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity) REMS processed (RDR) in situ environmental records for Gale crater spanning the early mission (order of the first ~1600 sols), providing physical-unit meteorology suitable for diurnal/seasonal water-activity analyses (e.g., converting humidity with respect to ice to liquid-relative humidity and screening for near-eutectic temperature/humidity windows).

Assemble MSL Curiosity REMS raw (EDR-level) time-series from Gale crater spanning the first ~1648 sols, specifically the relative humidity sensor measurements referenced to ice together with simultaneous ground temperature sensor readings, to reconstruct near-surface water vapor pressure and quantify nighttime latent-heat/enthalpy behavior using 1/Tg versus ln(PH2O) slope fits binned over multi-sol intervals.

Compile MSL Curiosity REMS processed (RDR-level) environmental records in physical units for Gale crater over the early multi-year traverse, including corrected air temperature/relative humidity and ground IR brightness temperatures, to test humidity–temperature crossings relevant to calcium-perchlorate deliquescence and to map seasonal/diurnal windows (e.g., around Ls ~100) when near-surface liquids could be thermodynamically permitted.

Retrieve Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity REMS calibrated meteorology in physical units from Gale crater (ground temperature plus near-surface air temperature and relative humidity) suitable for deriving near-surface water vapor pressure and for validating coupled 1-D subsurface heat–mass transfer simulations.

Retrieve Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity REMS raw engineering/science telemetry from Gale crater to independently reprocess the relative humidity and ground temperature sensors (including assessing short-timescale sensor self-heating effects) prior to computing water vapor pressure time series.
